patterns.vi: Tôi có thể làm gì đó.
examples: I can swim very well.
I can play the piano.
I can speak English.

patterns.pattern: Can you + V? - Yes, I can. / No, I can't.
patterns.vi: Bạn có thể... không? - Có, tôi có thể. / Không, tôi không thể.
examples: Can you bake cupcakes? - Yes, I can.
Can you do karate? - No, I can't.
Can you juggle three balls? - Yes, I can.

patterns.pattern: He/She can + V, but he/she can't + V.
patterns.vi: Cậu/Cô ấy có thể... nhưng không thể...
examples: Nam can draw, but he can't paint.
Mai can dance, but she can't sing.
Ben can ride a bike, but he can't skate.
I am good at playing chess.
She is good at cooking meals.
They are good at singing songs.

patterns.pattern: When I was five, I could + V.
patterns.vi: Khi tôi 5 tuổi, tôi đã có thể...
examples: When I was five, I could ride a bike.
When I was six, I could swim fast.
When she was four, she could draw birds.

patterns.pattern: When I was young, I couldn't + V.
patterns.vi: Khi tôi còn nhỏ, tôi đã không thể...
examples: When I was four, I couldn't speak English.
When he was three, he couldn't skip rope.
When we were young, we couldn't dive deeply.

patterns.pattern: Who can + V + faster / better / higher?
patterns.vi: Ai có thể... nhanh hơn / tốt hơn / cao hơn?
examples: Who can swim faster, Minh or Nam?
Who can jump higher in your class?
Who can play guitar better?

patterns.pattern: Next year, I will learn how to + V.
patterns.vi: Sang năm, tôi sẽ học cách...
examples: Next year, I will learn how to perform tricks.
Next summer, I will learn how to dive.
Next month, I will learn how to bake.

grammar.title: Can and Can't for Present Ability
grammar.explain_en: We use 'can' to talk about things we are able to do now, and 'can't' (cannot) for things we cannot do.
grammar.explain_vi: Dùng 'can' để nói về khả năng hiện tại và 'can't' cho những việc chưa thể làm.
examples: I can speak English clearly.
My brother can play chess very well.
She can't swim in deep water yet.

grammar.title: Could and Couldn't for Past Ability
grammar.explain_en: We use 'could' to describe abilities in the past, often with time expressions like 'when I was five'.
grammar.explain_vi: Dùng 'could' và 'couldn't' để diễn tả khả năng hoặc những gì không thể làm trong quá khứ.
examples: When I was six, I could ride a bicycle.
Two years ago, he couldn't speak English.
Could you swim when you were young?
grammar.right: ✅ When I was five, I could run fast.
grammar.wrong: ❌ When I was five, I can run fast.

grammar.title: Expressing Talents with 'Good at + V-ing'
grammar.explain_en: When expressing a strong talent, we use 'be good at' followed by an '-ing' verb or a noun.
grammar.explain_vi: Dùng cấu trúc 'be + good at + V-ing' để diễn tả sự thành thạo, giỏi giang ở một kĩ năng nào đó.
examples: Linh is good at painting colorful flowers.
We are good at playing basketball.
Are you good at cooking standard dishes?

grammar.title: Simple Comparatives for Skills (faster, higher, better)
grammar.explain_en: To compare how well people perform actions, add '-er' to short adverbs or use 'better'.
grammar.explain_vi: Dùng dạng so sánh hơn của trạng từ (như faster, higher, better) để so sánh kĩ năng giữa hai người.
examples: Nam can run faster than Tom.
Mai can jump higher than her brother.
An plays piano better than I do.
grammar.right: ✅ He can swim faster than me.
grammar.wrong: ❌ He can swim more fast than me.

readings.title: MAI'S JOURNEY OF LEARNING NEW SKILLS
readings.text:
Learning new abilities takes time, practice, and patience. Mai is a bright nine-year-old girl living in Hanoi. When Mai was five years old, she couldn't ride a bicycle without small training wheels. She fell down many times on the paved path in the park. However, Mai didn't give up. She tried again every afternoon after school. By age seven, she could ride smoothly and balance perfectly. 

Today, Mai has new goals. She is learning how to speak English fluently and play chess strategically. In English class, she can answer complex questions faster than before. Her teacher says she is getting better every week because she reads short stories every evening. In chess, Mai can plan three moves ahead, although her older brother An can still beat her because he is older and has played longer.

Next year, Mai will join the school swimming club to learn how to dive safely. She believes that anyone can acquire wonderful new talents if they work hard every day. Mai says, 'When I was younger, I couldn't do many things. Now I can do much more, and in the future, I will learn even more exciting skills!'

classroom_game.name: Talent Bingo Challenge
steps_en: Each student receives a 3x3 Bingo grid with action pictures (swim, play guitar, bake, skate, juggle, etc.).
Students walk around the room and ask classmates: 'Can you [action]?' or 'Could you [action] when you were five?'
If a classmate answers 'Yes, I can' or 'Yes, I could', they write that classmate's name in the matching grid square.
The first student to get three names in a row (horizontal, vertical, or diagonal) shouts 'BINGO!'
The winner presents the three talents and classmates' names to the whole class using target sentence patterns.
steps_vi: Mỗi học sinh nhận một phiếu Bingo 3x3 có hình vẽ các hoạt động (bơi, chơi ghi-ta, nướng bánh, trượt pa-tin, tung hứng, v.v.).
Học sinh đi quanh lớp và hỏi các bạn: 'Can you [hoạt động]?' hoặc 'Could you [hoạt động] when you were five?'
Nếu bạn trả lời 'Yes, I can' hoặc 'Yes, I could', học sinh viết tên bạn đó vào ô vuông tương ứng trên phiếu.
Học sinh đầu tiên hoàn thành 3 ô hàng ngang, hàng dọc hoặc đường chéo hô 'BINGO!'
Người thắng cuộc trình bày 3 năng khiếu cùng tên các bạn trước cả lớp bằng mẫu câu đã học.
